title: Submitting files to Sandbox and out-of-band inspection (Discan)

prose.text: Two SDK calls push a file to Sandbox outside the normal download path. {{submit}} {{submit-needs-rule}} {{daily-quota}} Reading the result is covered in [[zia.sandbox.report]], and the rule fields in [[zia.sandbox.rules]].
{{automate-publication}} Whether the two routes still work on a tenant is open {{gap:submission-route-status}}.

checks.do: Whether a clean Discan result is read as no known-bad signal, not as a detonation verdict, since Discan includes no dynamic analysis.
Whether the submit and Discan routes work on the target tenant before a customer is promised them.

submit.statement: The submit call sends a raw or archive file for full analysis (up to 100 files per day). Files are scanned by Zscaler antivirus and sent to the sandbox; the `force` parameter makes the sandbox reanalyze a file that already has a verdict. The verdict is read afterwards from the report endpoint.

quotes: You can submit up to 100 files per day
you can use the 'force' parameter to make the sandbox to reanalyze it
After files are sent for analysis, you must use GET /sandbox/report/{md5Hash} in order to retrieve the verdict.

submit-needs-rule.statement: A file whose type is not covered by the default policy rule is analyzed only if a Sandbox policy rule includes that file type; otherwise the response shows "Unknown".

quotes: If not, an 'Unknown' message is shown in the response.

discan.statement: Discan submits a file for out-of-band inspection that yields a real-time verdict for known and unknown files, using Malware Prevention, Advanced Threat Prevention, the Sandbox cloud effect, AI/ML analysis and third-party threat intelligence. It supports the file types of the Malware Protection and ATP policies, limits each file to 400 MB, and includes no dynamic file analysis, so it cannot catch what only detonation reveals. The Go SDK calls it `Discan` (POST /zscsb/discan); the Python SDK calls it `submit_file_for_inspection`.

quotes: Sandbox cloud effect, AI/ML-driven file analysis, and integrated third-party threat intelligence feeds
each file is limited to a size of 400 MB
Note: Dynamic file analysis is not included in out-of-band file inspection.

automate-publication.statement: The public Automate capture no longer lists `POST /zscsb/submit` or `POST /zscsb/discan`; the pinned Go and Python SDKs still construct both paths. This shows a gap between publication and clients, not that the backend routes were retired.
automate-publication.conditions: The removal from the capture is stated by the capture notes. That it says nothing about the backend is an inference: a capture drop is not a retirement notice, and no tenant test is vendored.

daily-quota.statement: Advanced Sandbox allows 100 API file submissions per day by default; the quota can be raised through the Zscaler account team or Support.

quotes: By default, Advanced Sandbox allows for 100 API file submissions per day. This quota can be raised by contacting your Zscaler Account team or Zscaler Support.

submission-route-status.title: Whether /zscsb/submit and /zscsb/discan still work on a tenant
submission-route-status.detail: The routes are absent from the public operation pages but present in both SDKs. Validate against the target tenant before treating them as current.

dynamic-analysis-duration.title: Unverified legacy statement: dynamic analysis takes 3 to 10 minutes
dynamic-analysis-duration.detail: Unverified legacy statement: The earlier reference gave this range. The only timing in the sources is the Go SDK's note that a report is available 10 minutes after submission.
